title: KDP Accepted, Apple Books Rejected? Here's Why
excerpt: Your EPUB cleared Amazon KDP but Apple Books rejected it. This happens more often than you'd think — here's the exact reason and how to fix it before your next upload.
meta_title: Apple Books Rejected My EPUB But KDP Accepted It — Here's Why | BookKraft AI
meta_description: KDP accepts EPUBs that Apple Books rejects because Amazon converts your file first. Learn the 6 most common reasons Apple Books rejects EPUBs and how to fix each one.
html:
You upload your EPUB to KDP, it goes live, everything looks fine. Then you try Apple Books Connect and get a rejection email. Same file. Different result.

This is one of the most frustrating things about wide publishing. Apple Books rejected your EPUB — not because it's a bad book, but because Apple has stricter technical requirements than Amazon. Here's what's actually happening and how to fix it.

Why KDP Accepts Files That Apple Books Rejects

Amazon KDP doesn't read your EPUB the way Apple Books does. KDP converts your EPUB into its own internal format before publishing. During that conversion, it silently fixes or ignores many structural problems.

Apple Books renders your EPUB directly. It's delivered to iOS and macOS devices as-is, which means every HTML error, every OPF problem, and every CSS conflict reaches the reader. Apple validates more strictly because it has to.

The same EPUB can fail Apple Books validation while passing KDP precisely because Amazon is doing repair work behind the scenes that Apple doesn't do.

The 6 Most Common Reasons Apple Books Rejects EPUBs

1. Invalid or Missing EPUB 3.0 Metadata

Apple Books requires proper EPUB 3.0 metadata in the OPF file. This includes a valid unique identifier, the correct EPUB version declaration, and a conforming dc:language tag. EPUB 2.0 files and poorly formed metadata frequently trigger rejections.

Check your content.opf for this declaration at the top:

<package xmlns="http://www.idpf.org/2007/opf" version="3.0">

If it says version 2.0, your file needs to be upgraded or rebuilt to EPUB 3.0 spec.

2. CSS That References External Resources

Apple Books blocks external resource loading. If your CSS contains @import url() references to Google Fonts or any external stylesheet, Apple will reject the file. All fonts and stylesheets must be embedded inside the EPUB package.

3. Malformed HTML in Chapter Files

Apple Books requires XHTML — not regular HTML. XHTML is stricter: every tag must be closed, attribute values must be quoted, and the file must be well-formed XML. A single unclosed <br> instead of <br/> is enough to cause a parse failure.

Run your EPUB through the EPUB Validator to catch every malformed tag before uploading to Apple.

4. Missing or Incorrect Navigation Document

EPUB 3.0 requires an nav.xhtml navigation document separate from the NCX file. This navigation document must include a toc nav element with links to every chapter. Many older conversion tools create only an NCX file, which is EPUB 2.0 format. Apple Books requires the EPUB 3.0 nav document.

5. Images That Exceed Size Limits

Apple Books enforces image size limits. Cover images over 4MB, or interior images over 2MB, frequently trigger rejections. High-resolution images from photography or illustration need to be compressed before embedding. A 300 DPI image saved at full quality for print is almost always too large for ebook delivery.

6. Incorrect Mimetype File

Every EPUB must contain a mimetype file as the very first file in the ZIP archive, stored without compression, containing exactly the text application/epub+zip. If the mimetype file is compressed, missing, or stored in the wrong position, Apple Books rejects the file immediately — often with a vague error message that doesn't mention mimetype at all.

How to Fix an Apple Books Rejection

The first step is getting a detailed validation report. Apple's rejection emails are often generic — they tell you the file was rejected but not which specific error caused it.

Upload your EPUB to the BookKraft AI EPUB Validator. It runs the same structural checks Apple Books uses and gives you a line-by-line breakdown of every problem. You'll know exactly what to fix before you upload again.

For EPUB 2.0 files that need to be upgraded, or files with heavy HTML errors throughout, the cleanest fix is often to rebuild from your manuscript using a proper EPUB 3.0 formatter rather than patching dozens of individual issues. The EPUB Formatter generates valid EPUB 3.0 output from your manuscript file — clean HTML, proper navigation, correct metadata, embedded CSS — without the errors that converters leave behind.

Before Your Next Upload

Always validate before uploading to any platform. A quick validation run catches rejections before they happen. Apple Books doesn't give you unlimited upload attempts — too many rejections can slow down your review process.

Also check your images. If any image file inside your EPUB is larger than 2MB, compress it. For cover images, aim for under 3MB. Apple has published specific guidelines — a cover image at 72 DPI, 1400px wide, saved as JPEG at 85% quality will always pass.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Apple Books tell you why an EPUB was rejected?

Sometimes, but not always. The rejection email often gives a category (like "metadata error" or "content error") without specifying which file or line caused the problem. Using a validator before uploading is much faster than decoding rejection emails.

Can I use the same EPUB file for KDP and Apple Books?

Yes, if the EPUB meets EPUB 3.0 spec. A properly formed EPUB 3.0 file works on both platforms. The problem is that KDP's tolerance for errors makes it easy to publish a file that isn't actually valid — and you only find out when you try Apple Books.

How long does Apple Books review take after fixing errors?

Usually 24–72 hours for new submissions. If you've had multiple rejections on the same ISBN, it can take longer. Fixing all validation errors before resubmitting — not just the ones mentioned in the rejection — is the fastest path through review.

Do I need separate metadata for Apple Books?

The metadata inside your EPUB OPF file is used for ingestion, but Apple Books Connect has its own metadata fields. Make sure your title, author, and ISBN match between your EPUB OPF and your Apple Books Connect entry — mismatches can cause ingestion errors even if the EPUB itself validates cleanly.

Is EPUB 2.0 accepted by Apple Books?

Apple Books technically supports EPUB 2.0, but many EPUB 2.0 files fail validation because of other structural issues that weren't caught at the time. Publishing in EPUB 3.0 is safer — it's the current standard and is what Apple Books is optimized for.
